Why It Matters

A Claim Is Only as Strong as Its Evidence

Prepared by a Registered Surveyor

A RISM-registered professional's report carries far more weight than a homeowner's complaint

Instrument Readings, Not Adjectives

"Very damp" is an opinion; a recorded moisture value is evidence

Organised Evidence Pack

Defects, photos, readings and chronology arranged so your case is easy to follow

Chronology & Correspondence

Guidance on documenting what you reported, when, and how the developer responded

Honest About Your Position

If an item is weak or within tolerance, we say so — surprises in a hearing help nobody

Consultation Before You File

Understand what your report supports before you commit to a claim

How It Works

4 Stages of Tribunal Support

We prepare the technical evidence and documentation — you present a case that stands up

1

Case & Document Review

We review your defect list, prior reports and correspondence with the developer

2

Evidence Inspection

Re-inspection focused on the disputed items, with instrument readings recorded

3

Documentation Pack

Report formatted for submission — findings, evidence and chronology in order

4

Consultation & Guidance

We walk you through the technical findings so you can present them clearly

Dated Photographic Evidence

Location-tagged

What It Includes

Instrument Readings

Objective values

What It Includes
Moisture percentages recordedElectrical test valuesCrack widths measuredCalibration traceable to SIRIM
Why It Counts

Chronology of Events

The timeline matters

What It Includes
Date of handover and DLP periodWhen each defect was reportedDeveloper's responses and delaysRe-inspection outcomes
Why It Counts
Shows you acted within time and the developer did not respond adequately

Reference to Standards

Not just personal opinion

What It Includes
Workmanship compared to accepted practiceTolerance limits referencedDistinguishes defect from tolerance
Why It Counts
Anchors your claim to a recognised benchmark, not a preference
